editorial.headline: Private Clinics: Open Nationally, Unblocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This code covers private clinical care from primary services to specialist settings, with full foreign-ownership capacity nationally and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
Private Clinic Activities covers the provision of primary and/or advanced health services through outpatient and/or inpatient care. It is framed as a privately organised activity, whether run by an individual or a business entity. The scope is broad within clinical practice: it includes primary and main clinics, occupational health clinics serving workers in support of workplace health efforts, and private health clinics specifically for athletes. It also identifies a PMA-supporting primary-clinic activity.

The code is open to businesses at every listed scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the record does not impose a foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity at the national level. That openness applies to an activity defined by the delivery of clinical services, not merely by the building or brand through which those services are offered.

Bali requires its own reading, because the province permanently blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. This code, however, is not marked as blocked. The stated reason is that, at the Besar scale, its OSS risk classification is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi; the record expressly concludes that it is therefore not blocked by the moratorium. Bali’s status is consequently not a contradiction of the national position: the national field sets the foreign-ownership ceiling, while the Bali field confirms that this code is not stopped by the province-wide PMA moratorium.

For a founder, the useful conclusion is precise rather than dramatic. A private clinic undertaking that genuinely fits this stated clinical scope may be structured across the listed business scales, with full foreign ownership available nationally. In Bali, the activity is not blocked for PMA registration by the moratorium. The large-scale OSS risk position explains that Bali outcome; it does not alter the underlying clinical scope, which remains centred on outpatient or inpatient primary and advanced care, including the occupational-health and athlete-clinic settings expressly named in the record.
editorial.pullQuote: The key distinction is simple: this code is fully foreign-open nationally and not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
